newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Five killed in Karachi violence.
newsitem.headline: Five killed in Karachi violence.

text.p: Two policemen, a navy employee and a political activist were killed overnight and on Wednesday in separate incidents in the Pakistani port city of Karachi, police said.
They said two policemen patrolling the central district's North Nazimabad area on motorcyles were apparently ambushed by unidentified gunmen and died instantly.
The mutilated body of a civilian employee of the Pakistan Navy, Mohammad Fayyaz, was found in the Mominabad area in the west of the city after being reported missing the night before.
Police said they suspected he had been kidnapped, tortured and then stabbed to death. They declined to speculate about the motive.
An activist of the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM) was killed in a drive-by shooting while he was standing outside his home in the Sharifabad area of central Karachi.
Police said they had also found the bullet-riddled body of an unidentified man in the same area on Tuesday night.
Violence has surged in Karachi in recent weeks in renewed feuding between the militants of the MQM and its breakaway Haqiqi faction.
At least 145 people have died in ethnic, sectarian and political violence in Karachi this year compared to about 500 in the whole of last year and more than 2,000 in 1995.
The MQM was brought into a coalition government in Sindh province, of which Karachi is the capital, after national and provincial elections in February.
